to.current_state: AI accelerator and networking demand is 'very strong' with revenue accelerating, but the first confirmed competitor-move evidence has arrived: on 2026-09-12 Reuters reported Marvell won a hyperscaler custom ASIC design win that had been expected to go to Broadcom (confirmed, direct fact; AVGO fell 3.9% on the news per indexed reporting). This is direct counter-evidence to Broadcom's assumed hold on custom AI silicon sockets. The program's revenue scale, customer identity, and whether Broadcom was formally in contention remain unquantified, so share gains vs. overall market growth is still unresolved — but competitor risk to the accelerator franchise is no longer hypothetical.

to.name: Custom AI ASIC share erosion (Marvell / hyperscaler insourcing)
to.statement: Hyperscalers progressively dual-source or insource custom AI silicon. Following the 2026-09-12 Marvell hyperscaler custom ASIC win (a program Broadcom was expected to supply), additional custom accelerator programs are competitively awarded to Marvell or designed in-house, capping Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue below the guided doubling trajectory and compressing the premium multiple at the same time. Registered as a downside scenario only — the base case is unchanged on a single data point.

questions_after.why_it_matters: Materiality for Broadcom's AI revenue trajectory hinges on whether this was a lost socket in Broadcom's pipeline or a program it never had; neither the program size nor Broadcom's formal involvement is established in th…

questions_after.question: Does the Marvell win reflect a deliberate hyperscaler dual-sourcing policy for custom AI silicon, and are further custom accelerator programs expected to be competitively awarded rather than defaulted to Broadcom?
questions_after.why_it_matters: A single design win is idiosyncratic; a sustained dual-sourcing policy would structurally cap Broadcom's share of custom AI silicon and would materially strengthen the share-erosion scenario.
